query: Summarise the circumstances of the fatal accident at Wegenhoft Plant (Texas) on October 20, 2021 (machinery): who was involved and what happened.
gold: On October 20, 2021, at approximately 9:35 a.m., the miner, a 50 year-old maintenance welder with nearly twelve years of mining experience, died when he was crushed between an excavator bucket and a telehandler.
answer:
On October 20, 2021, a 50-year-old maintenance welder with nearly twelve years of mining experience was fatally injured when he was crushed between the bucket of an excavator and a telehandler [E1]. The accident occurred because the mine operator did not maintain the excavator in safe operating condition [E1]. The excavator, a Volvo EC480EL Excavator with an 84-inch wide 5.5 yard bucket, had missing keeper bolts on the bucket connections, which caused the "dog bone" linkage to slip off, allowing the bucket to rotate forward and crush the miner [E5]. The miner was assisting in repositioning a hopper at the WP mine’s #1 Plant hopper [E2]. The pre-operational inspection of the excavator did not note any defects such as the missing keeper bolts [E4]. A Caterpillar TL1255D Telehandler was also involved in the accident [E5]. The miner had received task training on the telehandler and annual refresher training in accordance with MSHA Part 46 training regulations [E1][E2][E3][E5][E6].

query: For the fatal accident at Buchanan Mine #1 on August 20, 2014 (electrical), which 30 CFR standard did MSHA cite, and what does that standard require?
gold: 30 CFR 75.511 (Low-, medium-, or high-voltage distribution circuits and equipment; repair): [Statutory Provision] No electrical work shall be performed on low-, medium-, or high-voltage distribution circuits or equipment, except by a qualified person or by a person trained to perform electrical work and to maintain electrical equipment under the direct supervision of a qualified person.
answer:
MSHA cited 30 CFR § 75.511 for the fatal accident at Buchanan Mine #1 on August 20, 2014 [E1][E7]. This standard requires that no electrical work shall be performed on low-, medium-, or high-voltage distribution circuits or equipment, except by a qualified person or a person trained to perform electrical work under the direct supervision of a qualified person [E7]. Disconnecting devices must be locked out and suitably tagged by the persons performing the work, except when locking out is not possible, in which case the devices shall be opened and suitably tagged [E7]. Locks or tags shall be removed only by the persons who installed them or, if unavailable, by persons authorized by the operator or his agent [E7].
